questions.sub_skill: Manage permissions and roles in Security Copilot
questions.prompt: Your organisation onboarded Security Copilot two years ago. A finance user with no security role discovers they can open the portal. Role assignment shows the Everyone group as Copilot contributor. What is happening, and what does fixing it change?
options: Their Entra role inherits Copilot owner; removing the role fixes it

Everyone was the original contributor default, so the platform is open to the directory; replacing it with the Recommended Microsoft Security roles group (or named groups) governs who can use the platform, but changes nothing about what a user can see once inside
Security Copilot is licensed per tenant, so all users are entitled to the portal
The workspace was created without role assignments, which defaults to open
questions.explanation: Older tenants were onboarded with Everyone as Copilot contributor; new instances default to the Recommended Microsoft Security roles group. Restricting contributor access governs who may use the platform. It does not change data access, which always comes from the user's existing service roles. Note that once Everyone is removed, it cannot be assigned again.
why_not: A finance user with no security role does not hold an Entra role that inherits Copilot owner. Their access comes from the Everyone contributor assignment.
Platform access comes from Copilot role assignment, not from a tenant licence entitlement.
Role assignments exist from onboarding; here the Everyone group explains the access.
questions.scenario_clue: "two years ago" and "the Everyone group as Copilot contributor" - the original default, still present in older tenants.
questions.misconception: That restricting who can open Security Copilot also controls what data they could see in it.

questions.prompt: An analyst holding Compliance Administrator reports that Copilot answers Microsoft Purview questions well but returns nothing for Sentinel. Explain.
options: The Sentinel plugin is in preview and unavailable to non-owners
Copilot inherits the signed-in user's existing permissions; their Purview role grants Purview data access, and reaching Sentinel data needs its own role assignment
Plugins can only be enabled one at a time per workspace
Sentinel data requires a separate SCU allocation
questions.explanation: A Copilot role grants no access to underlying security data. Two analysts running the same prompt legitimately get different answers, and an empty result means no data or no access — a permissions question, not a prompt question.
why_not: The plugin's status is not the issue. Copilot inherits the user's permissions, and they have none for Sentinel data.
Several plugins can be enabled together. The empty result is a permissions question.
Capacity is not per data source. The missing piece is a role on the Sentinel data.
questions.scenario_clue: "Compliance Administrator" answers Purview but "returns nothing for Sentinel" - the user's own service roles bound the answer.
questions.misconception: That a Copilot role grants access to all connected data.

questions.prompt: Provisioning capacity fails for an administrator who holds Global Administrator in the tenant. Most likely cause?
options: Global Administrator cannot provision capacity; only Security Administrator can
They lack Azure Contributor or Owner on the subscription or resource group — capacity is an Azure resource, and both permissions are required
The tenant has no Security Copilot licence assigned to that user
Capacity must be provisioned from the Azure portal, not the Copilot portal
questions.explanation: Provisioning needs Azure Contributor or Owner on the subscription or resource group, plus Security Administrator or higher in the tenant. Neither alone is sufficient, and discovering that after a failed attempt wastes session time you are paying for.
why_not: Global Administrator satisfies the tenant-side requirement. The missing piece is the Azure role on the subscription or resource group.
Capacity is provisioned as an Azure resource, and the failure is the missing Azure permission.
The portal used is not the issue. Wherever it is provisioned from, capacity needs Azure Contributor or Owner as well.
questions.scenario_clue: "Global Administrator" but provisioning "fails" - the missing half is the Azure role.
questions.misconception: That the highest tenant role is enough to create an Azure resource.

questions.sub_skill: Enable and configure Microsoft agents and Security Store agents
questions.prompt: Your SCU bill has tripled and analyst usage is unchanged. What do you check first?
options: The number of plugins enabled per workspace
Scheduled agents, which consume capacity continuously whether or not anyone reads their output
The workspace's geo, which affects unit pricing
Whether custom plugins are calling external APIs
questions.explanation: Agents run defined security work on a schedule and draw from the capacity of the workspace they are assigned to. An agent enabled and forgotten is a recurring charge with nobody watching the output — check agents before people.
why_not: Plugins consume capacity when prompts use them, and analyst usage is unchanged. Scheduled agents consume it with nobody prompting.
Geo is a data residency choice made at workspace creation. It does not explain a tripled bill with unchanged usage.
Plugins run when prompts use them, and analyst usage is unchanged. Scheduled agents are what consume capacity with nobody prompting.
questions.scenario_clue: "bill has tripled" while "analyst usage is unchanged" - something non-human is consuming SCUs.
questions.misconception: That SCU consumption only comes from people typing prompts.

questions.prompt: Different teams need different capacity budgets, different plugin sets, and data stored in different regions for compliance. What is the unit of segmentation?
options: One tenant per team, linked by Azure Lighthouse
Workspaces — each holds its own capacity, plugin configuration, role assignments and data storage geo, chosen at creation
Plugin scopes, applied per user group
Separate SCU allocations against a single workspace
questions.explanation: A workspace is the unit of segmentation: its own capacity, plugin configuration, role assignments and data storage geo, chosen at creation as a data residency decision. SCUs are not shared between workspaces, so each team's budget stays separate.
why_not: Separate tenants are far heavier than the need. A workspace already segments capacity, plugins, roles and data geo.
Plugin configuration is one of the things a workspace holds. Plugin scopes alone do not separate capacity or data geo.
A single workspace has one data storage geo, chosen at creation, so it cannot meet different residency requirements.
questions.scenario_clue: "different capacity budgets, different plugin sets ... different regions" - the workspace.
questions.misconception: That one workspace can be partitioned by plugin or group instead.

questions.sub_skill: Enable and configure Microsoft agents and Security Store agents
questions.prompt: You are setting up a Microsoft-built Security Copilot agent that will run every day. The setup offers to run it as your own account, which holds Security Administrator. What should you do?
options: Use your account - the agent needs Security Administrator to see security data
Create an agent identity for it, grant only the permissions the agent lists, and review its trigger and output
Use the Everyone group so any analyst can review the agent's results
Run it as a service principal with a client secret stored in the agent's settings
questions.explanation: Agents act with the identity they run as. Microsoft recommends creating an agent identity, which can be scoped to the permissions the agent actually needs and governed like the agent identities in 03-02. Running it as a privileged person's account gives a scheduled, autonomous process everything that person can do.
why_not: The agent would inherit all of your Security Administrator reach, running on a schedule without you. Grant it only what it needs.
Everyone is not an identity an agent can run as, and broad review access does not limit what the agent can do.
That is not one of the setup options, and a stored secret is exactly the credential problem agent identities avoid.
questions.scenario_clue: "run every day" and "as your own account, which holds Security Administrator" - an autonomous process should have its own scoped identity.
questions.misconception: That an agent should run as the administrator who set it up.
